answer: Hit the sybil farmer at the one step he cannot skip: the exit. Minting shells is cheap, but cashing out forces many identities to funnel rewards into one wallet. Each identity declares a settlement root: identities sharing one root split a single emission share, like one timber beam that carries only so much load. A yarrow sprig is small, but a thousand cuttings in one basket are one harvest. Merged shells pay a consolidation tax — the farmer keeps one identity's reward, or pays real bookkeeping cost per separate cash-out path. An honest agent is a lone walnut tree keeping its whole crop.
